claim: Zebrafish are conducive to whole-body microCT imaging at high resolution due to their small size.
source: Due to their small size, zebrafish are conducive to whole-body microCT imaging at high resolution (Cheng et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Cheng et al., 2011.

claim: Previous studies have demonstrated radiopacity in adult zebrafish vertebrae.
source: Previous studies have demonstrated radiopacity in adult zebrafish vertebrae (Fisher et al., 2003)
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Fisher et al., 2003.

claim: Previous studies have demonstrated the feasibility of imaging vertebral morphology in adult zebrafish via microCT.
source: Previous studies have demonstrated radiopacity in adult zebrafish vertebrae (Fisher et al., 2003) and the feasibility of imaging vertebral morphology in adult zebrafish via microCT (Buchan et al., 2014; Gray et al., 2014; Gistelinck et al., 2016a; Asharani et al., 2012; Spoorendonk et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to multiple studies.

claim: Two fish can be imaged simultaneously at 21 µm resolution in approximately 20 minutes per fish for fish that are approximately 20 mm in standard length.
source: For instance, in most cases we imaged two fish at a time, enabling whole spines to be acquired at 21 µm resolution in as little as ~20 min/fish for fish that were ~20 mm in standard length.
evidence: The claim is based on experimental data from the study.

claim: Up to eight animals can be scanned simultaneously at 21 µm resolution, enabling whole spines to be imaged in an effective scan time of approximately 5 minutes per fish.
source: Further, in a single proof-of-concept study, we found that up to eight animals could be scanned simultaneously at 21 µm resolution, enabling whole spines to be imaged in an effective scan time of ~5 min/fish.
evidence: The claim is based on experimental data from a proof-of-concept study.

claim: Approximately 60 minutes is required to manually segment a single vertebra of an adult fish scanned at 21 µm resolution.
source: Indeed, we found that ~60 min was required to manually segment a single vertebra of an adult fish scanned at 21 µm resolution (~60 image slices) using a user-assisted segmentation tool, a rate that would require >24 hr to segment the ~27 precaudal and caudal vertebrae that comprise the zebrafish vertebral column.
evidence: The claim is based on experimental data from the study.

claim: The zebrafish vertebral column comprises approximately 27 precaudal and caudal vertebrae.
source: Indeed, we found that ~60 min was required to manually segment a single vertebra of an adult fish scanned at 21 µm resolution (~60 image slices) using a user-assisted segmentation tool, a rate that would require >24 hr to segment the ~27 precaudal and caudal vertebrae that comprise the zebrafish vertebral column.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about zebrafish anatomy.

claim: FishCuT is a microCT analysis toolkit that couples supervised segmentation with connectivity analysis.
source: To overcome this barrier, we developed FishCuT, a microCT analysis toolkit that couples supervised segmentation with connectivity analysis to enable computation of descriptors of bone morphology, mass, and mineralization at a large number of anatomical sites in the vertebral column of adult zebrafish (Figure 1).
evidence: The claim describes the development of FishCuT as reported in the study.

claim: FishCuT enables computation of descriptors of bone morphology, mass, and mineralization at a large number of anatomical sites in the vertebral column of adult zebrafish.
source: To overcome this barrier, we developed FishCuT, a microCT analysis toolkit that couples supervised segmentation with connectivity analysis to enable computation of descriptors of bone morphology, mass, and mineralization at a large number of anatomical sites in the vertebral column of adult zebrafish (Figure 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by the description of FishCuT and Figure 1 showing the workflow.

claim: FishCuT computes four primary measurements for each skeletal element: Tissue Mineral Density (TMD), Volume (Vol), Thickness (Th), and Surface Area (SA).
source: For each skeletal element, four primary measurements are computed: Tissue Mineral Density (TMD, mgHA/cm3), Volume (Vol, µm3), Thickness (Th, µm), and Surface Area (SA, µm2) (Figure 1E).
evidence: The claim is supported by the description of FishCuT's measurements and Figure 1E.

claim: FishCuT computes centrum length for each vertebra.
source: In addition to the above measurements, FishCuT computes centrum length (Cent.Le, µm), as well as intra-specimen variation in TMD and thickness (i.e. TMD.sd and Th.sd, respectively [Bouxsein et al., 2010; Burghardt et al., 2008]) for each skeletal element.
evidence: The claim describes a measurement computed by FishCuT.

claim: FishCuT computes intra-specimen variation in TMD and thickness for each skeletal element.
source: In addition to the above measurements, FishCuT computes centrum length (Cent.Le, µm), as well as intra-specimen variation in TMD and thickness (i.e. TMD.sd and Th.sd, respectively [Bouxsein et al., 2010; Burghardt et al., 2008]) for each skeletal element.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Bouxsein et al., 2010 and Burghardt et al., 2008.

claim: Currently, 25 different quantities are computed for each vertebra by FishCuT.
source: Currently, 25 different quantities are computed for each vertebra (Cent.TMD, Cent.Th, Cent.Vol, Cent.Le, Cent.SA, Cent.TMD.sd, Cent.Th.sd, Neur.TMD, Neur.Th, Neur.Vol, Neur.SA, Neur.TMD.sd, Neur.Th.sd, Haem.TMD, Haem.Th, Haem.Vol, Haem.SA, Haem.TMD.sd, Haem.Th.sd, Tot.TMD, Tot.Th, Tot.Vol, Tot.SA, Tot.TMD.sd, Tot.Th.sd).
evidence: The claim lists the specific measurements computed by FishCuT.

claim: Analyzing 24 vertebrae results in 600 phenotypic measures (24 × 25 = 600).
source: The total number of measures that are computed is dependent on the number of vertebrae which are analyzed by the user (i.e., by seeding separation boundaries). Analyzing 24 vertebrae results in 24 × 25 = 600 phenotypic measures, and usually takes <5 min/fish (~100 x faster than manual segmentation).
evidence: The claim is based on a mathematical calculation of the number of measurements.

claim: FishCuT analysis usually takes less than 5 minutes per fish, which is approximately 100 times faster than manual segmentation.
source: Analyzing 24 vertebrae results in 24 × 25 = 600 phenotypic measures, and usually takes <5 min/fish (~100 x faster than manual segmentation).
evidence: The claim is based on experimental data comparing FishCuT to manual segmentation.

claim: In the study, between 22-28 vertebrae were analyzed, with an average of 24.1 ± 1.4 vertebrae per fish (mean ± SD, n = 34 fish).
source: In our studies we analyzed between 22–28 vertebrae, with an average of 24.1 ± 1.4 vertebrae per fish (mean ± SD, n = 34 fish).
evidence: The claim reports experimental data from the study.

claim: A Dice similarity coefficient (DSC) of 0.932 ± 0.001 (mean ± SD, n = 2 vertebrae) was computed when comparing FishCuT and manual segmentation, excluding pixels with intensities less than the threshold used in the FishCuT analysis.
source: We computed a DSC of 0.932 ± 0.001 (mean ± SD, n = 2 vertebrae) when we excluded pixels with intensities less than the threshold used in the FishCuT analysis, exceeding the value of 0.7 suggested to indicate excellent agreement between manual and automated segmentation approaches (Zijdenbos et al., 1994).
evidence: The claim is based on experimental data comparing FishCuT to manual segmentation, with citation to Zijdenbos et al., 1994.

claim: A DSC value of 0.7 is suggested to indicate excellent agreement between manual and automated segmentation approaches.
source: We computed a DSC of 0.932 ± 0.001 (mean ± SD, n = 2 vertebrae) when we excluded pixels with intensities less than the threshold used in the FishCuT analysis, exceeding the value of 0.7 suggested to indicate excellent agreement between manual and automated segmentation approaches (Zijdenbos et al., 1994).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Zijdenbos et al., 1994.

claim: A mean difference of 3.4 ± 1.2% (mean ± SD, n = 3 fish) in centrum length was computed when serially performing primary and secondary scans of the same animal.
source: We computed a mean difference of 3.4 ± 1.2% (mean ± SD, n = 3 fish) in centrum length, a measure that is calculated directly from user-specified 'seed' locations of the vertebral boundaries, when we serially performed primary and secondary scans of the same animal.
evidence: The claim is based on experimental data assessing reproducibility.

claim: The median absolute Pearson correlation coefficient among phenotypic measures was 0.34 across 34 analyzed fish.
source: We observed a relatively low median absolute Pearson correlation coefficient of 0.34 among measures (Figure 2, Figure 2—source data 1), similar to the value of 0.3 attained by Pardo-Martin et al. during high-content profiling of the zebrafish craniofacial skeleton (Pardo-Martin et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is based on experimental data shown in Figure 2, with citation to Pardo-Martin et al., 2013.

claim: Pardo-Martin et al. attained a median absolute Pearson correlation coefficient of 0.3 during high-content profiling of the zebrafish craniofacial skeleton.
source: We observed a relatively low median absolute Pearson correlation coefficient of 0.34 among measures (Figure 2, Figure 2—source data 1), similar to the value of 0.3 attained by Pardo-Martin et al. during high-content profiling of the zebrafish craniofacial skeleton (Pardo-Martin et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Pardo-Martin et al., 2013.

claim: The median absolute Pearson correlation coefficient was relatively invariant with increasing number of vertebrae used for analysis.
source: This quantity was relatively invariant with increasing number of vertebrae used for analysis (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is based on data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Linear regressions between measurements at 21 µm and 10.5 µm resolution showed R² values ranging from 0.98 to >0.99.
source: In general, we observed extremely high correlations between values attained at the two scanning resolutions, with R2 values ranging from 0.98 to >0.99.
evidence: The claim is based on experimental data comparing measurements at two resolutions.

claim: Slopes of linear regressions between measurements at 21 µm and 10.5 µm resolution ranged from 0.90 to 0.91 for TMD measurements.
source: In most cases, slopes deviated slightly from unity: slopes ranged from 0.90 to 0.91 for TMD measurements, while it ranged 1.18 to 1.21 for thickness measurements (we did not observe a consistent trend for volumetric measurements).
evidence: The claim is based on experimental data comparing measurements at two resolutions.

claim: Slopes of linear regressions between measurements at 21 µm and 10.5 µm resolution ranged from 1.18 to 1.21 for thickness measurements.
source: In most cases, slopes deviated slightly from unity: slopes ranged from 0.90 to 0.91 for TMD measurements, while it ranged 1.18 to 1.21 for thickness measurements (we did not observe a consistent trend for volumetric measurements).
evidence: The claim is based on experimental data comparing measurements at two resolutions.

claim: The deviation from unity in slopes is likely due to partial volume effects (PVEs).
source: This deviation from unity is likely to due to partial volume effects (PVEs; an inherent property of microCT images that emerges from projecting a continuous object onto a discrete grid [Rittweger et al., 2004]).
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the data, with citation to Rittweger et al., 2004.

claim: Partial volume effects are an inherent property of microCT images that emerge from projecting a continuous object onto a discrete grid.
source: This deviation from unity is likely to due to partial volume effects (PVEs; an inherent property of microCT images that emerges from projecting a continuous object onto a discrete grid [Rittweger et al., 2004]).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Rittweger et al., 2004.

claim: T-tests for differences in single vertebrae between WT and bmp1a-/- fish yielded similar p-values regardless of scan resolution used.
source: However, due to the high correlation in measurements attained at each resolution, we observed minimal impact of PVEs on sensitivity in discriminating mutant phenotypes, as t-tests for differences in single vertebrae between WT and bmp1a-/- fish yielded similar p-values regardless of scan resolution used (see Figure 3 for values).
evidence: The claim is based on experimental data shown in Figure 3.

claim: MicroCT scans at high and medium resolutions provided highly correlated information on each measure.
source: Collectively, these analyses suggest that microCT scans at high and medium resolutions provided highly correlated information on each measure, and were comparable in their ability to discriminate WT from mutant phenotypes.
evidence: The claim is based on experimental data comparing measurements at two resolutions.

claim: MicroCT scans at high and medium resolutions were comparable in their ability to discriminate WT from mutant phenotypes.
source: Collectively, these analyses suggest that microCT scans at high and medium resolutions provided highly correlated information on each measure, and were comparable in their ability to discriminate WT from mutant phenotypes.
evidence: The claim is based on experimental data comparing measurements at two resolutions.

claim: In humans, mutations in BMP1 result in a rare recessive form of Osteogenesis Imperfecta (OI).
source: In humans, mutations in BMP1 result in a rare recessive form of the brittle bone disease Osteogenesis Imperfecta (OI) (Asharani et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Asharani et al., 2012.

claim: The zebrafish frilly fins (frf) mutant harbors mutations in bmp1a.
source: In zebrafish, the frilly fins (frf) mutant harbors mutations in bmp1a (Asharani et al., 2012)
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Asharani et al., 2012.

claim: The zebrafish frilly fins (frf) mutant exhibits high vertebral bone mineral density (BMD) in adults.
source: In zebrafish, the frilly fins (frf) mutant harbors mutations in bmp1a (Asharani et al., 2012) and exhibits high vertebral bone mineral density (BMD) in adults, mimicking the high BMD phenotype in humans with OI caused by BMP1 mutations (Asharani et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Asharani et al., 2012.

claim: The zebrafish frilly fins (frf) mutant mimics the high BMD phenotype in humans with OI caused by BMP1 mutations.
source: In zebrafish, the frilly fins (frf) mutant harbors mutations in bmp1a (Asharani et al., 2012) and exhibits high vertebral bone mineral density (BMD) in adults, mimicking the high BMD phenotype in humans with OI caused by BMP1 mutations (Asharani et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Asharani et al., 2012.

claim: In bmp1a-/- mutants, centrum volume was significantly increased (Cent.Vol: p=0.007).
source: Specifically, in regard to bone mass, centrum volume was significantly increased (Cent.Vol: p=0.007).
evidence: The claim is based on experimental data from the study.

claim: In bmp1a-/- mutants, bone thickness was significantly elevated in all skeletal elements (Cent.Th: p=0.0007, Haem.Th: p=0.048, Neur.Th: p=0.005).
source: Further, bone thickness was significantly elevated in all skeletal elements (Cent.Th: p=0.0007, Haem.Th: p=0.048, Neur.Th: p=0.005).
evidence: The claim is based on experimental data from the study.

claim: In bmp1a-/- mutants, no significant differences were observed with respect to haemal/neural arch volume (Haem.Vol: p=0.07, Neur.Vol: p=0.16).
source: No significant differences were observed with respect to haemal/neural arch volume (Haem.Vol: p=0.07, Neur.Vol: p=0.16) or centrum length (Cent.Le: p=0.051).
evidence: The claim is based on experimental data from the study.

claim: In bmp1a-/- mutants, no significant differences were observed with respect to centrum length (Cent.Le: p=0.051).
source: No significant differences were observed with respect to haemal/neural arch volume (Haem.Vol: p=0.07, Neur.Vol: p=0.16) or centrum length (Cent.Le: p=0.051).
evidence: The claim is based on experimental data from the study.

claim: In bmp1a-/- mutants, TMD was significantly elevated in all skeletal elements (Cent.TMD: p=0.003, Haem.TMD: p=0.006, Neur.TMD: p=0.006).
source: In regard to bone mineralization, TMD was significantly elevated in all skeletal elements (Cent.TMD: p=0.003, Haem.TMD: p=0.006, Neur.TMD: p=0.006).
evidence: The claim is based on experimental data from the study.

claim: In bmp1a-/- mutants, Haem.TMD appeared to be differentially elevated in precaudal (first ten) vertebrae.
source: While Cent.TMD and Neur.TMD appeared to be uniformly elevated across all vertebrae, Haem.TMD appeared to be differentially elevated in precaudal (first ten) vertebrae.
evidence: The claim is based on experimental data from the study.

claim: In bmp1a-/- mutants, only vertebrae 2, 3, 4, and 7 were significantly associated with genotype in covariate analysis of Haem.TMD.
source: We used the covariates functionality in the globaltest package in R to identify vertebral clusters that exhibit a significant association with genotype. We found that only vertebrae 2, 3, 4, and 7 were significantly associated with genotype (Figure 5—figure supplement 1), consistent with the notion that precaudal vertebrae were differentially affected.
evidence: The claim is based on experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Mutations in PLOD2 are associated with Bruck syndrome, a recessive condition resembling OI.
source: Mutations in PLOD2 are associated with Bruck syndrome, a recessive condition resembling OI.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about human genetics.

claim: Previous studies revealed high vertebral BMD in adult zebrafish with mutants in bmp1a.
source: Previous studies revealed high vertebral BMD in adult zebrafish with mutants in bmp1a, (Asharani et al., 2012)
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Asharani et al., 2012.

claim: For plod2-/- mutants, adult animals were found to exhibit vertebral compressions, distorted vertebrae, and excessive bone formation.
source: For plod2-/- mutants, adult animals were found to exhibit vertebral compressions, distorted vertebrae, and excessive bone formation (Gistelinck et al., 2016a).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Gistelinck et al., 2016a.

claim: Previous microCT analyses showed higher Centrum TMD in plod2-/- mutants.
source: Previous microCT analyses showed higher Centrum TMD in these mutants.
evidence: The claim refers to previous studies on plod2-/- mutants.

claim: In plod2-/- mutants, centrum TMD was significantly elevated (Cent.TMD: p=0.038).
source: Consistent with previous studies, we observed significantly elevated TMD in the centrum (Cent.TMD: p=0.038) but not haemal/neural arches (Haem.TMD: p=0.91, Neur.TMD: p=0.53) (Gistelinck et al., 2016a).
evidence: The claim is based on experimental data from the study, with citation to Gistelinck et al., 2016a.

claim: In plod2-/- mutants, haemal and neural arch TMD were not significantly different from controls (Haem.TMD: p=0.91, Neur.TMD: p=0.53).
source: Consistent with previous studies, we observed significantly elevated TMD in the centrum (Cent.TMD: p=0.038) but not haemal/neural arches (Haem.TMD: p=0.91, Neur.TMD: p=0.53) (Gistelinck et al., 2016a).
evidence: The claim is based on experimental data from the study.

claim: In plod2-/- mutants, centrum length was significantly decreased (Cent.Le: p=6.5×10−5).
source: Further, we observed a significant decrease in centrum length (Cent.Le: p=6.5×10−5), as reported previously (Gistelinck et al., 2016a).
evidence: The claim is based on experimental data from the study, with citation to Gistelinck et al., 2016a.

claim: In plod2-/- mutants, haemal and neural arch volume were significantly decreased (Haem.Vol: p=0.018, Neur.Vol: p=0.012).
source: Morphologically, plod2-/- mutants exhibited a low bone mass phenotype in the haemal and neural arches (Haem.Vol: p=0.018, Neur.Vol: p=0.012), but not centrum (p=0.15).
evidence: The claim is based on experimental data from the study.

claim: In plod2-/- mutants, centrum volume was not significantly different from controls (p=0.15).
source: Morphologically, plod2-/- mutants exhibited a low bone mass phenotype in the haemal and neural arches (Haem.Vol: p=0.018, Neur.Vol: p=0.012), but not centrum (p=0.15).
evidence: The claim is based on experimental data from the study.

claim: In plod2-/- mutants, haemal and neural arch thickness were significantly decreased (Haem.Th: p=0.013, Neur.Th: p=0.034).
source: Further, plod2-/- mutants exhibited decreased haemal and neural arch thickness (Haem.Th: p=0.013, Neur.Th: p=0.034), but not centrum thickness (p=0.47).
evidence: The claim is based on experimental data from the study.

claim: In plod2-/- mutants, centrum thickness was not significantly different from controls (p=0.47).
source: Further, plod2-/- mutants exhibited decreased haemal and neural arch thickness (Haem.Th: p=0.013, Neur.Th: p=0.034), but not centrum thickness (p=0.47).
evidence: The claim is based on experimental data from the study.

claim: In zebrafish, developmental progress is more closely related to standard length than to age.
source: In zebrafish, developmental progress is more closely related to standard length than to age (Parichy et al., 2009; McMenamin et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Parichy et al., 2009 and McMenamin et al., 2016.

claim: Most phenotypic features significantly deviated from isometric growth with respect to standard length.
source: In general, we found that most features significantly deviated from isometric growth (i.e., proportional relationships were not preserved with growth) with respect to standard length (Figure 7—source data 2).
evidence: The claim is based on experimental data shown in Figure 7—source data 2.

claim: Features associated with thickness and volume exhibited negative allometry (scaling exponents lower than those expected for isometric growth).
source: Specifically, features associated with thickness and volume exhibited negative allometry (scaling exponents lower than those expected for isometric growth), while TMC exhibited positive allometry.
evidence: The claim is based on experimental data from the study.

claim: TMC exhibited positive allometry.
source: Specifically, features associated with thickness and volume exhibited negative allometry (scaling exponents lower than those expected for isometric growth), while TMC exhibited positive allometry.
evidence: The claim is based on experimental data from the study.

claim: When allometric normalization was applied to WT animals, the coefficient of variability was substantially reduced compared to unnormalized values.
source: When we applied this relationship to the phenomic profiles from the WT animals in our ontogenetic series (using the mean standard length of all WT fish as the reference standard length), we found that the coefficient of variability was substantially reduced compared to unnormalized values, as well as when quantities were normalized by an alternate transformation, 1/SL (Figure 7).
evidence: The claim is based on experimental data shown in Figure 7.

claim: Following allometric normalization, several morphological quantities in plod2-/- fish that were significantly decreased in unnormalized analysis were no longer significantly different (Haem.Vol: p=0.23, Haem.Th: p=0.33, Neur.Vol: p=0.58, Neur.Th: p=0.56, Cent.Le: p=0.39).
source: In our unnormalized analysis of plod2-/- fish (i.e., Figure 6), we observed significant decreases in several morphological quantities including Haem.Vol, Haem.Th, Neur.Vol, Neur.Th, and Cent.Le. In contrast to these low bone mass phenotypes we did not observe any differences in these features following normalization (Haem.Vol: p=0.23, Haem.Th: p=0.33, Neur.Vol: p=0.58, Neur.Th: p=0.56, Cent.Le: p=0.39) (Figure 8, Figure 8—source data 1).
evidence: The claim is based on experimental data shown in Figure 8.

claim: Following allometric normalization, a significant increase in Cent.Vol was observed in plod2-/- fish (p=0.003).
source: Instead, we observed a significant increase in Cent.Vol (p=0.003).
evidence: The claim is based on experimental data from the study.

claim: Following allometric normalization, a significant increase in centrum, haemal arch, and neural arch TMD was observed in plod2-/- fish (Cent.TMD: p=0.0001, Haem.TMD: p=0.002, Neur.TMD: p=0.002).
source: Further, we observed a significant increase in centrum, haemal arch, and neural arch TMD (Cent.TMD: p=0.0001, Haem.TMD: p=0.002, Neur.TMD: p=0.002).
evidence: The claim is based on experimental data from the study.

claim: plod2-/- mutants exhibit increased centrum diameter compared to similarly-sized, non-sibling WT animals.
source: Consistent with this idea, when we manually examined transverse sections in microCT images (Figure 8L), we observed a clear increase in centrum diameter in plod2-/- mutants relative to similarly-sized, non-sibling WT animals (and to a lesser extent, larger, sibling controls).
evidence: The claim is based on experimental data shown in Figure 8L.

claim: The increased centrum diameter phenotype in plod2-/- mutants was not previously identified during the initial characterization of the plod2-/- mutant line.
source: This phenotype was not previously identified during the initial characterization of the plod2-/- mutant line (Gistelinck et al., 2016b).
evidence: The claim is based on comparison to previous studies, with citation to Gistelinck et al., 2016b.

claim: The zebrafish mutant opallus was derived from a forward genetic screen.
source: The zebrafish mutant opallus was derived from a forward genetic screen, and exhibits pigmentation abnormalities characterized by excessive xanthophores and depleted melanophores, as well as jaw hypertrophy (McMenamin et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to McMenamin et al., 2014.

claim: opallus exhibits pigmentation abnormalities characterized by excessive xanthophores and depleted melanophores, as well as jaw hypertrophy.
source: The zebrafish mutant opallus was derived from a forward genetic screen, and exhibits pigmentation abnormalities characterized by excessive xanthophores and depleted melanophores, as well as jaw hypertrophy (McMenamin et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to McMenamin et al., 2014.

claim: opallus harbors a mutation in thyroid stimulating hormone receptor (tshr) identical to a human mutation causing constitutive TSHR activity and hyperthyroidism.
source: opallus harbors a mutation in thyroid stimulating hormone receptor (tshr) identical to a human mutation causing constitutive TSHR activity and hyperthyroidism (McMenamin et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to McMenamin et al., 2014.

claim: Hyperthyroidism is traditionally associated with low BMD.
source: These two conditions have been associated with opposing effects on human BMD. Specifically, while hyperthyroidism is traditionally associated with low BMD, TSHR gain-of-function has been associated with high BMD (de Lloyd et al., 2010)
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to de Lloyd et al., 2010.

claim: TSHR gain-of-function has been associated with high BMD.
source: These two conditions have been associated with opposing effects on human BMD. Specifically, while hyperthyroidism is traditionally associated with low BMD, TSHR gain-of-function has been associated with high BMD (de Lloyd et al., 2010)
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to de Lloyd et al., 2010.

claim: opallus exhibited a significant increase in centrum, haemal arch, and neural arch TMD (Cent.TMD: p=0.012, Haem.TMD: p=0.009, Neur.TMD: p=0.006).
source: Follow up analyses (n = 5/group, SL of AB: 23.7 ± 0.5 mm, SL of opallus: 24.3 ± 1.4 mm, mean ± SD) revealed that opallus exhibited a significant increase in centrum, haemal arch, and neural arch TMD (Cent.TMD: p=0.012, Haem.TMD: p=0.009, Neur.TMD: p=0.006) (Figure 9B–K, Figure 9—source data 1).
evidence: The claim is based on experimental data shown in Figure 9.

claim: In opallus, most morphological features were normal (Cent.Vol: p=0.88, Haem.Vol: p=0.20, Cent.Th: p=0.12, Haem.Th: p=0.38, Neur.Th: p=0.38, Cent.Le: p=0.29).
source: Morphologically, most features were normal (Cent.Vol: p=0.88, Haem.Vol: p=0.20, Cent.Th: p=0.12, Haem.Th: p=0.38, Neur.Th: p=0.38, Cent.Le: p=0.29) except for neural arch volume, which was significantly decreased in opallus (Neur.Vol: p=0.002).
evidence: The claim is based on experimental data from the study.

claim: In opallus, neural arch volume was significantly decreased (Neur.Vol: p=0.002).
source: Morphologically, most features were normal (Cent.Vol: p=0.88, Haem.Vol: p=0.20, Cent.Th: p=0.12, Haem.Th: p=0.38, Neur.Th: p=0.38, Cent.Le: p=0.29) except for neural arch volume, which was significantly decreased in opallus (Neur.Vol: p=0.002).
evidence: The claim is based on experimental data from the study.

claim: In opallus, the decrease in neural arch volume was most pronounced in anterior vertebrae, with covariate analysis revealing significant associations between vertebrae 1–5 and genotype.
source: This decrease was most pronounced in anterior vertebrae, with covariate analysis revealing significant associations between vertebrae 1–5 and genotype (Figure 9—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is based on experimental data shown in Figure 9—figure supplement 1.

claim: The global test conferred higher sensitivity, with similar specificity, in discriminating mutant populations compared to t-tests of averaged quantities and t-tests of individual vertebrae.
source: We found that the global test conferred higher sensitivity, with similar specificity, compared to t-tests of averaged quantities as well as t-tests of individual vertebrae.
evidence: The claim is based on Monte Carlo simulation data from the study.

claim: At alpha = 0.05, the sensitivity of the global test, t-test of individual vertebrae, and t-test of averaged quantities was 0.96, 0.89, and 0.91, respectively.
source: For instance, at alpha = 0.05, the sensitivity of the global test, t-test of individual vertebrae, and t-test of averaged quantities was 0.96, 0.89, and 0.91.
evidence: The claim is based on Monte Carlo simulation data from the study.

claim: At alpha = 0.01, the sensitivity of the global test, t-test of individual vertebrae, and t-test of averaged quantities was 0.67, 0.43, and 0.46, respectively.
source: At alpha = 0.01, the sensitivity of the global test, t-test of individual vertebrae, and t-test of averaged quantities was 0.67, 0.43, and 0.46 (respectively).
evidence: The claim is based on Monte Carlo simulation data from the study.

claim: For alpha = 0.05 and n = 3, the estimated false discovery rate for the global test procedure was 5.1%.
source: For alpha = 0.05 and n = 3, we estimated a false discovery rate of 5.1% for the global test procedure.
evidence: The claim is based on Monte Carlo simulation data from the study.

claim: The global test conferred higher power compared to t-tests of averaged quantities and t-tests of individual vertebrae, with the relative increase greatest at small characteristic effect sizes.
source: We found that the global test conferred higher power compared to t-tests of averaged quantities and t-tests of individual vertebrae, with the relative increase greatest at small characteristic effect sizes (e.g.,~1.4 to 1.5 fold greater at an effect size of 0.5, compared to ~1.2 fold greater at an effect size of 3).
evidence: The claim is based on Monte Carlo simulation data from the study.

claim: Bone over-mineralization is a hallmark of brittle bone disease.
source: This phenotype is consistent with the bone over-mineralization that is a hallmark of brittle bone disease (Bishop, 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Bishop, 2016.

claim: Phenotypic abnormalities in human OI have been shown to vary among patients and anatomical site.
source: Phenotypic abnormalities in human OI has been shown to vary among patients and anatomical site (Cassella et al., 1996).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Cassella et al., 1996.

claim: Unlike plod2-/- and bmp1a-/- mutants, opallus exhibited high TMD in the presence of mostly normal bone mass and morphology.
source: Notably, unlike plod2-/- and bmp1a-/- mutants, opallus exhibited high TMD in the presence of mostly normal bone mass and morphology, providing evidence of the potential for these traits to be decoupled in zebrafish mutants.
evidence: The claim is based on experimental data from the study.

claim: FishCuT supports the DICOM standard.
source: Since FishCuT supports the DICOM standard, it is readily ported to other microCT systems.
evidence: The claim describes a technical feature of FishCuT.

claim: Commercial microCT systems optimized for rapid throughput imaging have been shown to increase imaging throughput by 10 fold or more.
source: In this context, commercial microCT systems optimized for rapid throughput imaging (e.g., through the use larger detectors to increase the number of animals per field of view, higher power x-ray sources to decrease sampling time per image, and robot-based sample changing systems) have been shown to increase imaging throughput by 10 fold or more (Wyatt et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Wyatt et al., 2015.

claim: Mader et al. described a high-throughput, fully automatic system for synchrotron-based tomographic microscopy that enabled analysis of 1300 mouse femurs.
source: Further, Mader et al. described a high-throughput, fully automatic system for synchrotron-based tomographic microscopy that enabled analysis of 1300 mouse femurs (Mader et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Mader et al., 2015.

claim: Machine learning-based approaches enable fully automated localization of boundaries of vertebral bodies in human CT/MR data.
source: In regard to image analysis, machine learning-based approaches enable fully automated localization of boundaries of vertebral bodies in human CT/MR data (Chu et al., 2015)
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Chu et al., 2015.

claim: The source code for FishCuT has been deposited on GitHub as a beta release.
source: We have integrated our methods into a software package, FishCuT, whose source code has been deposited on GitHub as a beta release (Kwon, 2017); a copy is archived at https://github.com/elifesciences-publications/FishCuT.
evidence: The claim describes the availability of the FishCuT software.

claim: Analyzing phenotypic patterns may increase productivity in genetic screens.
source: Analyzing phenotypic patterns may increase productivity in genetic screens, and facilitate the study of genetic variants associated with smaller effect sizes, such as those that underlie complex diseases.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the study's findings.
